## About
Modern Mower is a repair shop on Mound Rd. in Sterling Heights. We work on residential and commercial equipment: lawn mowers, snow blowers, riding mowers, zero turns and other equipment. Owner Brian Rismoen is still the lead technician. He started taking things apart as a kid and, in his words, is "a bit of a geek when it comes to engines, electronics, and just about anything mechanical."
Brian says everyone who works here has that same mechanical mind, and our customers mention them by name. One reviewer thanked Tim A. for servicing a mower that now runs better than it did out of the box. Another thanked Aaron for a new carburetor job. Another said Jose sharpened his blades while he waited.
We're rated 4.9 from 785 Google reviews. Just bring it in or schedule a pickup, and we'll get it diagnosed quickly.

## Services
- Lawn Mower Repair: Push mowers, riding mowers and zero turns. Just bring it in, we work on it here.
- Snow Blower Repair: Snow blower repair and service for homeowners in Sterling Heights and nearby.
- Commercial Equipment Repair: Repair for commercial equipment as well as residential machines.
- Unlimited Blade Re-sharpening: If we sharpen your blade or you buy a new blade from us, we'll resharpen it at no additional cost all season long, usually while you wait.
- Free Winterization with Any Tune Up: Have a tune up done here, bring the unit back at the end of the season during the recommended time, and we'll clean it out and get it ready for storage at no extra charge. Outside the recommended time, winterization costs extra.
- Pickup and Delivery Service: Not everyone owns a truck. Call us with your address for a quote and to set up a time. Additional units cost extra. ($70 round trip)

## FAQ
Q: How fast can you get my equipment done?
A: We can even get many done the same day if you bring it in early.

Q: Will I know the cost before you start?
A: Yes. We diagnose it quickly, sometimes within minutes, and let you know what it's going to cost before we do any work.

Q: Why should I winterize my mower?
A: Gas left in the machine, even a little, even if you run it until it dies, can damage the carburetor and keep it from running right or starting at all.
